newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates firm after jump in swaps.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates firm after jump in swaps.

text.p: Interbank rates were firmer on Friday after a jump in swap points, dealers said.
"Swaps have moved a lot to the right and this is pushing interbank rates higher," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank. "But I don't think rates can go much higher as the market is still flush."
On Thursday, one-month swaps soared from 17 to 50 points, and six-month from 160 to 250.

Dealers said the rise could be due to players building up long ringgit positions on the swaps for another speculative attack on the ringgit. Such a position would allow speculators to sell ringgit without worrying about a potential squeeze by Bank Negara, they said.
Dealers said there was talk that the central bank might impose some restriction on the ringgit forwards next week, which would effectively create a two-tier market.
They said there was some perception that speculators would turn their attention to the ringgit after having achieved some partial gains on the baht.
One-week money was at 7.00/50 percent against 6.40/50 on Thursday.
One-month money was at 7.50/60 percent from 7.25 percent, and three-month was also at 7.50/60 percent against 7.35/40.
The overnight rate was expected to remain at 5.50 percent as maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Friday would add to market liquidity.
But there will be some tightness next week due to a one-billion ringgit bill issue.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mostly unchanged.
At 0330 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was steady at 92.58, or an implied yield of 7.42 percent.
The December contract was unchanged at 92.73, or 7.27 percent and March 1998 was also unchanged at 92.74, or 7.26 percent.
